On Wed, Jul 22, 2026 at 09:20, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Andre — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. I'm escalating to Eng and we've opened a ticket (Zendesk #5681).

Quick triage summary (initial):
- Root cause (likely): sudden request-distribution shift from a handful of Acme instances caused many small requests to land on the same worker, causing the runtime's batching heuristic to form large batches and increase internal queue depth. The combination increased head-of-line blocking and raised p95/p99.
- Evidence: worker-level queue depth spikes, increased batch sizes (avg batch size x4 for ~7m), KV cache hit steady (so not a model slowdown).
- Impact: p95/p99 spikes and transient 5xx errors as queue timeouts were hit.

Immediate mitigations we are applying (in the next 10–15m):
1) Force immediate flush on small prompt sizes for the Acme routing key (temporary override).
2) Reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 24 for affected pool and lower queue-depth threshold to 120ms.
3) Expand worker pool by +2 nodes in us-west-2 (hot-add); also enable emergency fallback to the lower-latency model variant if queue depth remains high.

I've pushed a hotfix config (rolling across the pool) and attached traces (engineer_traces_20260722.zip). Early telemetry shows queue depth falling and p95 improving. I'll post a full postmortem once stable.

Sean Gallagher
